name: Trees
description: A tree is a hierarchical structure with a root and child nodes. Binary trees have at most two children per node; binary search trees (BST) keep left < node < right, enabling O(log N) average search. Trees are ideal for recursive and divide-and-conquer solutions.
key_points: Traversals: inorder, preorder, postorder, and level-order (BFS).
Inorder traversal of a BST yields sorted output.
Height of a balanced tree is O(log N), of a skewed tree O(N).
Many tree problems are naturally recursive: solve left, solve right, combine.
common_mistakes: Not handling the null node base case in recursion.
Confusing left/right subtree results and losing them before combining.
